definitions.full: H1765. dachaph [ דָּחַף ] verb drive, hasten (late) (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic דְּחַף ) — Qal Passive participle plural דְּחוּפִים of runners Est 3:15 ; 8:14 (|| מְבֹהָלִים ). Niph`al Perfect hasten one's self, hurry אֶלֿ נִדְחַף Est 6:12 ; לָצֵאת נִדְחַף 2Chr 26:20 (|| בהל ).

occurrences.englishText: Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked at him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out quickly from there. Yes, he himself also hurried to go out, because Yahweh had struck him.
The couriers went out in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city of Susa was perplexed.
Mordecai came back to the king’s gate, but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and having his head covered.
So the couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. The decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.
